subject.name_or_desc: A prisoner escaped out of prison (the quesited); the querent unnamed

context.question: A prisoner escaped out of prison — which way did he go? If recoverable?
context.setting: The prisoner had broken out of prison; the querent asked which way he had gone and whether he would be recovered.

attachments.key_positions: The person of the prisoner represented by the cusp of the twelfth (Sagittarius) and by Jupiter in Leo; the sign of the twelfth, the sign wherein Jupiter is, the quarter of heaven, and the sign wherein the Moon is, unanimously eastward; the Moon neer the Ascendant; Jupiter in the eighth house; the Moon separating from a trine of Jupiter and applying to an opposition of the Sun, both in angles; Jupiter and Mercury in aspect with each other
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. XCV: a prisoner escaped out of prison — which way he went, if recoverable (Fig. 29 in the 1852 Zadkiel edition)
